papers.title: Spectral Landmarks: Alignment of Landmark Kernel Translates with the Leading Eigenfunctions of a Kernel Operator
papers.abstract: We study the problem of choosing $m$ landmark points so that the span of the kernel translates is as close as possible to the leading $s$-dimensional eigenspace of a positive-definite kernel. The natural measure is the Hilbert-Schmidt operator discrepancy between the reproducing-kernel-Hilbert-space (RKHS) projectors onto the two subspaces. We give a closed form spectral alignment function in terms of the truncated Mercer kernel and relate it to the classical integrated power function (Nystr\"om trace error) through a two-sided sandwich bound. Minimizing the function by gradient descent on the landmark coordinates produces landmark sets that are evenly spaced. Theoretical results show that optimal configurations are those whose eigenfunction sampling matrix is a scaled isometry. On homogeneous spaces these are exactly the minimal equal-weight cubature rules for products of leading eigenfunctions, and for every $m\ge s$ they are the configurations whose sampled eigenfunctions form a unit-norm tight frame. Experiments on $\mathbb{S}^1$ and $\mathbb{S}^2$ agree with the theory. On the circle, with $s\le2m$ and a moderate bandwidth, every random start converges to equispaced landmarks, and on the sphere the optimizer recovers the regular tetrahedron, octahedron, and icosahedron from random starts. Finally, we analyze the numerical conditioning of the problem.

papers.title: Higher Integrability of Differential Form Globally Solving Certain Minimization Problem
papers.abstract: Let $0\leq k\leq n-1,1<p<\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}\left(B;\Lambda^k\right)$, where $\Lambda^k$ is the vector space of all $k$-forms in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $B$ is an open ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In this article, with one global higher integrability assumption on $du$, we study the global higher integrability of $dv$ where $v$ is the unique minimizer of the following functional: \begin{align*} \overline{w}\mapsto \int_{B} \left \lvert d\overline{w} \right \rvert^p \text{ where } \overline{w} \in u+W^{1,p}_{d^*,T}\left(B;\Lambda^{k}\right). \end{align*} As a machinery, with a similar higher integrability assumption on the $k+1$-differential form $\widetilde{F}$, we prove one local higher integrability of $d\widetilde{W}$ where $\widetilde{W}\in W^{1,p}\left(B_r\left(0\right);\Lambda^{k}\right)$ weakly solves: \begin{align*} d^*\left(\left \langle G \left(d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right), d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right \rangle^{\frac{p-2}{2}}G \left(d \widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right)\right)=0 \text{ in } B_r\left(0\right), \end{align*} for $G:B_r\left(0\right)\rightarrow GL\left({n\choose k+1};\mathbb{R}\right)$ symmetric, bounded, and uniformly elliptic measurable map, which is sufficiently close to the identity map $I:\Lambda^{k+1}\rightarrow \Lambda^{k+1}$. For each of the above mentioned cases, we prove one strong $\left(q,q\right)$ type estimate. As the primary tools, we use the Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality, Fefferman-Stein inequality, and one classical regularity result of K. Ulhenbeck.

papers.title: On K\"onig's non-existence conjecture for the one-dimensional fractional Bianchi-Egnell inequality
papers.abstract: K\"onig conjectured that the sharp stability constant in the Bianchi-Egnell inequality for the one-dimensional fractional Sobolev inequality equals the local stability constant and that the associated quotient has no minimizer outside the set of optimizers of the fractional Sobolev inequality. We prove both assertions for $s<1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, with an explicitly computable threshold. The proof is based on a reinterpretation of the Frank-Lieb rigidity mechanism. Due to the lack of smooth variational structure of the Bianchi-Egnell quotient, we work with a refined limiting inequality of Beckner-Onofri-type on the circle with vanishing first-order moments, which we derive from Toeplitz determinants.

papers.title: Boundedness properties of bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate mapping properties on Lebesgue spaces of bilinear Fourier integral operators (FIOs) with complex phases. Indeed, we provide for bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases boundedness theorems for the corresponding Seeger-Sogge-Stein orders, including the endpoint estimates. Our results extend the same boundedness property in the case of real-valued phases proved by Rodriguez-L\'opez, Rule, and Staubach, and provide the bilinear version for the linear one proved earlier by Ruzhansky for phases of positive type. Also, our Seeger-Sogge-Stein theorem for bilinear operators with complex phases cannot be directly deduced from its real counterpart. A new approach used in this article consists of providing directly the boundedness theorems on Lebesgue spaces without the use of the multilinear Fefferman-Stein interpolation theorem. For this, a maximal function theorem due to Bourgain is applied. As a byproduct, we also consider transference boundedness theorems of FIOs with complex phases from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to the torus $\mathbb{T}^n\equiv \mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ and then, we provide new criteria for the boundedness of Fourier integral operators on the torus with complex phases (Fourier series operators in the sense of Ruzhansky and Turunen).

papers.title: Sharp angle estimates for second order divergence operators
papers.abstract: This article is about the (minimal) sector containing the numerical range of the principal part of a linear second-order elliptic differential operator defined by a form on closed subspaces $V$ of the first-order Sobolev space $W^{1,2}(\Omega)$ incorporating mixed boundary conditions. We relate the angle of sectoriality and the $\mathcal{H}^\infty$-angle of realizations of the elliptic operator to two reference angles: the optimal angle of the $L^2$-realization and the optimal angle of the coefficient function. We thereby consider the operator in several scales of Banach spaces: the Lebesgue space, the negative Sobolev space, and their interpolation scale. For the latter two types of spaces, we rely on recent results regarding the Kato square root property. We focus on minimal assumptions on geometry, and we consider both real and complex coefficients, in particular aiming at explicit estimates built on readily accessible problem data. New results include an explicit estimate for the angle of sectoriality for the elliptic operator on $L^p(\Omega)$ with complex coefficients without any assumptions on geometry, which reduces to the known sharp angle for real coefficients, a new estimate on the angle of the sector containing the numerical range of a linear, continuous and coercive Hilbert space operator, and an estimate on the $\mathcal{H}^{\infty}$-angle for the elliptic operator on $L^p(\Omega)$ with real coefficients.

papers.title: Operator Fej\'{e}r-Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial $F\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)[x]$ positive semidefinite on $K$ admits a certificate in the operator quadratic module generated by $S$, with weighted degree at most $\operatorname{deg} F+c_S$. Here, $c_S$ depends only on $S$ and is independent of both $F$ and the coefficient Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, which may be infinite-dimensional. In contrast to the scalar case, natural matrix preorderings admit no uniform degree bound over compact semialgebraic subsets of the real line. We construct positive semidefinite quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees tend to infinity as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap remains bounded below. Conversely, uniform degree bounds hold for interval unions in a fixed compact interval when the component and gap lengths are bounded below by positive constants. Our proofs develop two techniques. The first is a quadratic reduction principle that reduces the problem of obtaining degree bounds for arbitrary-degree operator polynomials to the quadratic case, with a fixed additive increase in degree. The second uses a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil to transfer positivity on unions of intervals to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fej\'er-Riesz theorem provides certificates. We also obtain operator-valued Fej\'er-Riesz factorizations on unions of circular arcs, rational certificates with a fixed denominator on unbounded semialgebraic sets, and a characterization of the sets whose natural operator preorderings admit degree-preserving certificates.

papers.title: Nondoubling Calder\'on-Zygmund theory across geometries
papers.abstract: We develop a Calder\'on--Zygmund theory without the doubling property, a metric or a martingale structure. Our measure spaces carry an exhausting family of admissible sets with recursive child partitions. A stopping-time construction gives a decomposition of an integrable function, with a bounded good part and bad terms that cancel on the parents of the stopping sets. We introduce the corresponding atomic Hardy and BMO spaces, establish their duality and interpolation properties, and prove weak-type $(1,1)$ and Hardy-space bounds for singular integral operators under a H\"ormander condition and a size estimate between each stopping set and its parent. We apply this framework to arbitrary flow trees, whose associated flow measures need not be either locally or globally doubling. As a result, we obtain endpoint bounds for Riesz transforms and spectral multipliers satisfying a scale-invariant Sobolev condition of order greater than $3/2$ in this setting.

papers.title: Interpolation, Factorization, and Approximation in the Numerical Radius Unit Ball
papers.abstract:
We initiate a systematic study of Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and function theory for matrix-valued holomorphic functions on the unit disk taking values in the numerical radius unit ball - a class we term as $
u$-Schur functions. In contrast to the operator-norm setting, where commutatnt lifting reduces interpolation to the positivity of a single Pick matrix, we show that a natural one-parameter familty of Pick-type matrices arising from Ando's characterization is necessary but not sufficient for solvability. We overcome this obstruction by establishing two necessary and sufficient solvability criteria. The first is constructive, resting on a factorization of $
u$-Schur function $F=PGQ$ into a classical Schur function $G$ and bounded holomorphic matrix functions $P, Q$ coupled by a boundary condition. This yields an accompanying Choi-Li-type dilation representation. The second is dual and geometric, characterizing solvability via a Nehari-type distance from a cononical model-space interpolant to a subspace determined by the interpolation data. Finally, we introduce $
u$-inner functions - $
u$-Schur functions whose non-tangential boundary values lie almost everywhere in the set of extremal numerical contractions - and prove that every non-extremal problem admits a $
u$-inner solution. As a consequence, we obtain a numerical-radius Caratheodory approximation theorem: $
u$-inner functions are dense in the $
u$-Schur class under the compact-open topology.

papers.title: Multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for Banach space valued holomorphic functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study a generalized notion of multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for holomorphic functions defined on the unit ball of the finite-dimensional Minkowski sequence space with values in complex Banach spaces. We first prove that the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius is positive for every non-null bounded linear operator whose norm is sufficiently small relative to the scaling parameter. We then determine the exact asymptotic behavior of the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces of finite cotype and we obtain analogous bounds for spaces without finite cotype. Finally, for concave Banach lattices and summing operators, we prove lower bounds that involve a logarithmic factor. These results connect classical scalar Bohr phenomena with operator-valued and Banach space valued settings, and highlight how the geometry of the spaces and the mapping properties of the operator influence coefficient estimates and their dependence on dimension. Several examples illustrate the consistency of our results with the classical Bohr radius and the sharp Defant--Frerick asymptotics.

papers.title: A Kreiss theorem for fractional Cauchy problems with a finite slow component
papers.abstract: Fractional Cauchy problems with a Caputo derivative of order bounded by one are solved by Mittag-Leffler operator families that lack the semigroup property but remain bounded for classes of sectorial generators, even with spectrum in the right half-plane. To study their transient growth we introduce the fractional Kreiss constant via the Laplace transform of the propagator family. For a closed generator on a Banach space with a time-scale separation and a finite spectral component, that is, a finite-rank projector commuting with the generator whose complement carries a bounded family, we prove that the projected part of the propagator (typically slow spectral part carrying dynamics that is pertinent at mid and long time-scales) is comparable to a deflated Kreiss constant up to a factor linear in the rank, uniformly in fractional order and independently of the dimension. The analytic core of this result is a Bernstein-type inequality for a class of non-rational functions on vertical lines proved by bounding the turning of the derivative. This is a fundamentally different technique from the classical one used in Kreiss theorem for Markov semigroups based on counting intersections of algebraic curves. Importantly, we show that the rank dependence cannot be removed while keeping the Kreiss constant upper bound. Finally, we show that in Hilbert spaces, generators whose numerical range avoids the sector of instability obey the sharp bound of normal operators, which no spectral-set estimate improves. To conclude, we discuss how subdiffusion driven by a self-excited oscillator, the time-fractional Schr\"odinger equation, and time-changed Markov dynamics illustrate the theory.

papers.title: A counterexample to the Jordan tuple conjecture of Ball and Helton
papers.abstract: This article constructs a pair of bounded commuting 3-symmetric operators with no Jordan-family extension. The operators are coordinate multipliers on a Sobolev space of functions with values in three dimensional complex Euclidean space with an equivalent Hilbert norm. Their quadratic symbol has no operator polynomial factorization, even with an auxiliary target Hilbert space. The construction transfers the nonfactorability of the matrix quadratic used by Russo to the symbol of a commuting 3-symmetric tuple. The factorization approach of McCullough--Russo and Russo then supplies the obstruction to a Jordan-family extension.

papers.title: Lower bounds for the Kolmogorov widths of global attractors of dissipative systems
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of a strengthening set in a Hilbert space and prove an exponential lower bound for its Kolmogorov widths. For compact sets containing the origin, the strengthening property is equivalent to the existence of such a bound. As an application, we obtain an exact formula for the widths of the global attractor of a diagonal dissipative system.

papers.title: Spaces with maximal monotone convex subdifferentials
papers.abstract: We characterize the real Hausdorff locally convex spaces on which every proper lower semicontinuous convex function has a maximal monotone convex subdifferential. Equivalent conditions are given in terms of the portability of closed convex sets and identities involving upper envelopes. Among normed spaces, this property is equivalent to completeness; among Fr\'echet spaces, it is equivalent to normability. We also prove that the property is preserved under products with finite-dimensional spaces.

papers.title: Invariance of Arens module actions on the norm dual of a Riesz-normed f-algebra
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an f-algebra and let $V$ be an order ideal of its order dual $A^{\sim}$ that separates the points of $A$. In a comment accompanying a theorem of Huijsmans and de Pagter (J. Funct. Anal. 59 (1984), 41--64), it is stated that the proof of that theorem can easily be adapted to show that the order continuous dual $V_n^{\sim}$ of $V$ is an f-algebra under the Arens multiplication. We show that this statement is false. The Arens multiplication on $V_n^{\sim}$ requires two invariance conditions on $V$, with respect to the module actions of $A$ and of $V_n^{\sim}$, which do not follow from the stated hypotheses and can fail already in the most natural case, where $A$ carries a Riesz norm and $V=A^$ is the norm dual of $A$. We prove that the first condition holds if and only if $A$ is bounded, and that the second holds whenever the Riesz norm is submultiplicative (which forces $A$ to be bounded); in that case $(A^)_n^{\sim}$ is indeed an f-algebra. We then construct a bounded f-algebra of finitely supported real sequences, equipped with a non-submultiplicative Riesz norm, for which the second condition fails, so that the Arens multiplication on $(A^*)_n^{\sim}$ is not even defined. The comment has also been used in the literature to derive a further result, which is false as well. This clarifies the exact scope of the comment.

papers.title: Lau's Fixed Point Problem for Elementary Amenable Groups and Finite Left Amenable Semigroups
papers.abstract: Lau's fixed point conjecture is proved for elementary amenable groups. More generally, a weak$^*$-continuous nonexpansive representation of such a group on a nonempty weak$^*$-closed nonexpansive retract of a weak$^*$-compact convex subset $C$ of a dual Banach space has a nonempty common fixed point set that is a nonexpansive retract of $C$. For finite left amenable semigroups, continuity and weak$^*$-closedness of the retract are unnecessary. The argument also leads to a new class of amenable groups with the same retraction property, which contains all elementary amenable groups and may be strictly larger. This class may provide a useful framework for further research on Lau's conjecture. Bruck's theorem is also extended from abelian to elementary amenable group actions on nonexpansive retracts of weakly compact convex sets with the fixed point and conditional fixed point properties, without weak continuity, thus partially answering a longstanding question of Bruck. Several consequences of the theorem are recorded.

papers.title: A simple proof of the characterization of $\ell_\infty^n$ by norm-one projections and a stability estimate
papers.abstract: We give a short and elementary proof of a classical fact that an $n$-dimensional real or complex normed space with the absolute projection constant equal to one is linearly isometric to $\ell_\infty^n$. The proof uses only finite-dimensional convexity and linear algebra, with no infinite-dimensional ingredients. The same approach yields a quantitative stability estimate of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{3}}$ when the absolute projection constant is at most $1+\varepsilon$. This improves Zippin's estimate of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{8}}$ in each fixed dimension as $\varepsilon \to 0$. The real and complex cases are treated by the same arguments.

papers.title: A remark on the entropy numbers of mixed smoothness classes
papers.abstract: We find the right orders of both the entropy numbers and the Kolmogorov widths of classes of multivariate functions with bounded mixed derivative, when the class is defined by the restriction in the uniform norm and the error of approximation is measured in the uniform norm. The case of functions of two variables was settled about 30 years ago and the case of three or more variables stayed open.

papers.title: Schatten isometries of Grassmann spaces
papers.abstract: We characterize all (not necessarily surjective) Schatten $p$-isometries of the Grassmann space of rank $k$ projections on a complex Hilbert space for every $p\in(0,\infty]$. We prove that every such isometry is induced by a linear or conjugate-linear isometry of the underlying Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, with the additional possibility of composition with orthocomplementation when $\dim \mathcal H = 2k > 2$. Our result generalizes Wigner's theorem, which plays a central role in the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics. It also extends previous results on Schatten $p$-isometries of Grassmann spaces, including characterizations of surjective isometries by Geh\'er and \v{S}emrl for $p=\infty$ and by Qian et al. for $0<p<\infty$ and that of not necessarily surjective isometries by Geh\'er for $p=2$.

papers.title: Finite sums of weighted composition operators on the Fock space
papers.abstract: We study finite sums of weighted composition operators on the classical Fock space. We show that no cancellation phenomenon occurs when the composition symbols are pairwise distinct: such a sum is bounded, compact, or belongs to the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<\infty, if and only if each summand has the corresponding property. We also obtain two-sided essential norm estimates and quantitative Schatten norm comparisons for fixed distinct nonconstant symbols. As an application, we obtain corresponding boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class results for finite sums of generalized Volterra-type integral operators.

papers.title: Dynamical frames through Sz.$-$Nagy$-$Foias dilations
papers.abstract: We present a unified operator-theoretic treatment of dynamical frames based on defect operators, Stein equations, and the Sz.-Nagy-Foia\c{s} dilation theory of contractions. An explicit realization of the minimal isometric dilation relates generating vectors to the wandering subspace and provides a geometric interpretation of standard frame constructions. For Parseval dynamical frames, polar decomposition yields a complete factorization of the generating families through the adjoint defect operator. General dynamical frames are described in terms of positive solutions of a Stein equation, leading to an equivalent formulation of the frame index. We also collect characteristic-function criteria for strong stability and joint strong stability. In the diagonal case, the characteristic function expresses the classical separation and Carleson conditions in operator-theoretic terms. The emphasis is on explicit constructions, direct proofs, and a common framework for known results.

papers.title: Isometries for Hilbert's metric on vector lattices of continuous functions
papers.abstract: In this paper Hilbert's projective metric on the interior of the positive cone of an Archimedean vector lattice with a strong order unit is studied. We show that every surjective isometry between two such projective cones is induced by a lattice isomorphism, possibly composed with the inversion map, and that the inversion occurs precisely when the vector lattice is a bounded inverse closed $f$-algebra. In particular, two such projective cones are isometric if and only if the underlying vector lattices are lattice isomorphic, and we determine the corresponding isometry groups. We apply these results to spaces of H\"older continuous functions, absolutely continuous functions, and continuous functions of bounded variation, for which we describe the surjective isometries explicitly. Finally, we show that the projective cones of these spaces of functions on an interval all have the same metric completion, but that no two of them are isometric.

papers.title: Totally Positive Interpolation and Critical Sampling of Positive Operator Orbits
papers.abstract: How few observations are needed for the stable recovery of the initial state of a linear dynamical system? We study this question for systems governed by a positive operator, with fixed sensors and freely chosen sampling times and positive weights. Our main tool is an interpolation theorem for translates of a nonzero continuous integrable totally positive function. For every uniformly separated sequence of centers, we choose one node near each center so that the corresponding collocation operator is boundedly invertible. The displacement, node separation, and operator bounds depend only on the kernel and the lower separation of the centers; no upper bound is needed on their gaps. If a single integer orbit is a frame, we construct weighted Riesz bases whose sampling counts attain the spectral lower bound up to a bounded additive error. The same method yields bases from continuous functional calculus, including explicit resolvent bases. In the case of normal operators, we give a single-orbit frame for which every admissible weighted design has sampling count growing faster than the radial spectral count.

papers.title: Higher-Order Isometric Liftings of Convex and Concave Operators
papers.abstract: We study higher-order isometric liftings of bounded operators on Hilbert spaces under convexity and concavity assumptions. First, we prove that every $m$-convex operator $T$ satisfying $\sup_{n\geq 1}n^{-(m-1)}\|T^n\|^2<\infty$ admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting whose complementary diagonal entry is an expansive $(m-1)$-isometric weighted shift. Next, we show that every $m$-concave operator admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting with an expansive $m$-isometric weighted-shift component, without imposing an additional growth assumption. We also establish an alternation between convexity and concavity under polynomial growth conditions and give examples illustrating limitations of converse implications.

papers.title: The numerical index with respect to a Lipschitz map
papers.abstract: We introduce the Lipschitz numerical range, radius, and index with respect to a norm-one Lipschitz map, unifying the Lipschitz numerical index of a Banach space and the numerical index with respect to an operator. For real-valued maps, we obtain metric formulas on finite metric spaces and graphs. In particular, a connected simple unweighted graph with at least two vertices is bipartite if and only if its real Lipschitz-free space, or equivalently its dual, has classical numerical index one. We also characterize finite metric spaces by universal numerical-radius attainment. Among complete metric spaces, we characterize length spaces by non-denseness of maps attaining their $g$-Lipschitz numerical radius for every norm-one $g$. Moreover, we derive upper bounds for the $g$-Lipschitz numerical index with $\ell_p$ targets, $1<p<\infty$, and lower bounds for the Lipschitz numerical index of spaces with property $\beta$. Finally, for norm-one operators $G: X \to Y$ between real Banach spaces, we prove $$ n_{G^*}(Y^*,X^*) \leq n_{L,G}(X,Y) \leq n_G(X,Y), $$ with equality in the upper bound whenever $X$ is separable or $Y$ is $1$-complemented in its bidual. This extends recent equality results for the identity operator to arbitrary norm-one operators and a broader class of target spaces.

papers.title: Isospectral Density Design and Distinct Global Shape Transitions in Weighted Yukawa Droplets
papers.abstract: We study Euclidean perimeter plus Yukawa repulsion with a fixed radial source density and a fixed ordinary volume. For each sufficiently small positive screening parameter, we construct two smooth, positive, strictly increasing densities whose constrained shape Hessians at the unit ball agree for every coupling. Their source masses, Yukawa moments, and ball self-energies also agree. Just above their common first global transition threshold, all minimizers form one rotation orbit of tetrahedral shapes for one density and one orbit of sectoral threefold shapes for the other. Both transitions are continuous, and the minimizing shapes are strictly convex. We obtain the two densities by fixing the boundary data that determine the Hessian and changing the higher derivatives that determine the reduced quartic energy. We compute a positive quartic coefficient, restore the three scalar observables by interior corrections, and add a finite exterior density barrier to control all finite-perimeter competitors.

papers.title: Schauder bases and local unconditional structure in Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series
papers.abstract: We prove that among the Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series with $1\le p<\infty$, only $\mathcal{H}^2$ has local unconditional structure. Consequently, $\mathcal{H}^p$ admits an unconditional basis exactly when $p=2$. At the endpoint $p=1$, we also construct a Schauder basis of Dirichlet polynomials and give an explicit formula for each basis vector. Together, these results answer the basis questions posed by Aleman, Olsen and Saksman, as well as the question of Saksman and Seip concerning an unconditional basis for $\mathcal{H}^1$.

papers.title: Linear Dynamics of Composition Operators on Zygmund Spaces of Rooted Trees
papers.abstract: We conjugate composition operators on the Zygmund and little Zygmund spaces of an infinite, locally finite rooted tree $T$ by the second-difference isometries. A path Green kernel gives row-finite matrices that characterize boundedness and yield exact operator norms. A rigidity result holds on the chain $\mathbb{N}_0$. Boundedness on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is equivalent to $\varphi(n)=qn+b$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with $q\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and $b\in\mathbb{Z}$. For these symbols, $\varphi(n)>n$ eventually characterizes Li-Yorke chaos of $C_\varphi$ on either Zygmund space, allowing noninjectivity and periodic vertices. If $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $\mathcal{Z}_0(T)$ and $\varphi^k(T)$ eventually avoids every finite set, then for each $\lambda\ne0$, $\lambda C_\varphi$ is Li-Yorke chaotic on either space exactly when the norms of its powers are unbounded. For $\varphi_q(n)=q(n+1)-1$ with integer $q\ge2$, the corresponding conditions are $|\lambda|q^2>1$ on both Zygmund spaces and $|\lambda|q>1$ on the little Lipschitz space. For bounded $C_\varphi$ on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$, topological mixing and Devaney chaos each hold exactly for injective symbols with no periodic vertices and eventual slope $q\ge2$. For such bounded operators with strictly increasing $\varphi$ and $\varphi(0)>0$, $q\ge2$ also characterizes hypercyclicity and frequent hypercyclicity.

papers.title: Entropy and frame measures for self-affine measures
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a real expanding $d\times d$ matrix and let $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\R^d$ consist of $N\ge2$ distinct vectors. We study the existence of frame measures for the self-affine probability measure $\mu$ generated by the maps $S_i(x)=M^{-1}(x+d_i)$ with equal weights $1/N$. Extending the entropy obstruction for self-similar measures with a common scalar contraction, we prove that $\mu$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy of the first symbol given the spatial point is positive. In particular, this holds whenever $N>|\det M|$, without assuming absolute continuity or imposing arithmetic conditions. When $M$ has integer entries, $\mathscr D\subset\Z^d$, and $N=|\det M|$, the measure $\mu$ admits a frame measure if and only if $\mu$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor.

papers.title: Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality implies superreflexivity
papers.abstract: We prove that if \(X\) is a Banach space for which Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality holds, then \(X\) is superreflexive. We also present an example of a superreflexive Banach space for which the vector-valued Stein property fails.

papers.title: Preserver Problems for Products of Operator Differences
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate surjective maps $\Phi:\mathscr B(H)\to\mathscr B(H)$ preserving various operator quantities associated with products of differences, namely, $$\alpha\big((\Phi(A)-\Phi(B))\Phi(C)\big) =\alpha\big((A-B)C\big) \quad \text{for all}~ A,B,C\in\mathscr B(H),$$ where $\alpha$ denotes one of the following: the numerical radius, maximal numerical range, minimum modulus, surjectivity modulus, reduced minimum modulus, or spectral radius. Under suitable assumptions, we establish structural characterizations of these maps and determine their possible forms.
